events.text: Magazine began publication in Saint Petersburg.
Pletnyov took over as editor after Pushkin's death.

evidence.quote: Pyotr Pletnyov took over the editorship in 1838

events.text: Pletnyov handed the magazine over to Nekrasov and Panaev.

evidence.quote: Pletnyov handed it over to Nikolay Nekrasov and Ivan Panaev in 1847

events.text: Chernyshevsky succeeded Belinsky as the magazine's leading critic.

evidence.quote: Belinsky was succeeded by Nikolai Chernyshevsky in 1853

events.label: political turn
events.text: Magazine entered polemics and turned into a political magazine.

evidence.quote: In late 1858 , the magazine entered into polemics

events.label: polemic
events.text: Began polemic with Herzen's Kolokol over aims of Russian democracy.

evidence.quote: In 1859-1861 , Sovremennik argued with Herzens Kolokol about the aims of the Russian democracy

events.text: Published materials dedicated to serf emancipation.

evidence.quote: In 1861 , it published materials , dedicated to the emancipation of the serfs
an 8-month suspension of publishing activities ( in June 1862 )

events.text: Nekrasov resumed publication of the magazine.

evidence.quote: In 1863 , Nekrasov managed to resume publishing Sovremennik

events.text: Nekrasov invited Saltykov-Shchedrin, Antonovich, Yeliseyev and Pypin to editorial staff.

evidence.quote: In 1863 , Nekrasov managed to resume publishing Sovremennik . He invited Mikhail Saltykov-Shchedrin

events.text: Published Chernyshevsky's What Is to Be Done? and plebeian authors' works (1863-1866).

evidence.quote: In 1863-1866 , Sovremennik published Chernyshevskys What Is to Be Done ?

events.label: closure
events.text: Magazine closed down amid official panic after attempt on Alexander II.

evidence.quote: The magazine was closed down in June 1866
